function: Learns pilot-data power allocation per resource element and refines LS channel estimates with a CNN for superimposed-pilot uplink multiuser MIMO (p. 2; p. 3).
system: Uplink multiuser MIMO-OFDM: BS with M=64 antennas, K=12 single-antenna users, 192 subcarriers, 30 kHz spacing, 2.6 GHz carrier; no RIS (p. 2; p. 4).
method: SIPNet: learnable sigmoid power factors and 7-layer CNN refining LS estimates, supervised gradient-descent training on mean pilot power plus channel MSE; non-learned ICEDD receiver (p. 3; p. 4).
data_channel: 3GPP CDL-A from a link-level ULSCH/PUSCH simulator; 900 training samples, delay spreads 100 to 300 ns, a specific mobility velocity, random user locations; no public dataset (p. 4).
test_conditions: Training: Es/sigma^2 2 to 5 dB, delay spread 100 to 300 ns, 3 or 60 km/h; test: 200 ns delay spread, Es/sigma^2 sweep, different user locations (p. 4).
baselines: Non-learned: traditional 5G NR DM-RS pilot scheme, existing SIP with iterative receiver [5], and data-interference-free bound; no learned baseline (p. 4).
metrics: Sum throughput in Mbps versus Es/sigma^2, from cyclic redundancy check per transport block; learned power-factor distributions (p. 4; p. 5).
complexity: Order per ICEDD iteration O(N_RE K^2 M + N_RE K Q_m log2 Q_m + N_MP N_b N_RE K log2 Q_m); CNN cost not reported (p. 4).
openness: none; training data self-generated, no code or data link (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "the 3GPP CDL-A channel" - the link-level ULSCH/PUSCH simulator runs under CDL-A (3GPP TR 38.901 profile), which generates the training samples and the test channels.
q2_support: p. 4: "user location setting, which differs from those used when" - held-out user locations of the same CDL-A model; the 200 ns test delay spread lies inside the 100 to 300 ns training range (Table II); no new scenario, band, or dataset.
q3_support: p. 4: "We consider the traditional pilot (TP) scheme, the existing" - the compared schemes are TP, SIP with iterative receiver [5], and SIP perfSub, all non-learned; no earlier learned method (such as [10], [11] cited on pp. 1-2) is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "a computational complexity per iteration of" - gives O(N_RE K^2 M + N_RE K Q_m log2 Q_m + N_MP N_b N_RE K log2 Q_m) for the ICEDD receiver of the proposed scheme; the CNN cost is not reported.
q5_support: p. 4: "total of 900 channel samples as training data, considering" - the training channels come from the authors' own simulator; no code or data link, public dataset, or measurement is given.
notes: Area 2: the learned parts are the pilot-data power factors and the CNN refinement of the LS channel estimate; the ICEDD data detection is not learned (p. 2, p. 3). q2 borderline: test user locations differ from training (p. 4) but come from the same CDL-A model, and A* is reported per mobility scenario (p. 5). q4 borderline: the stated order covers only the ICEDD receiver, not the CNN.
